name: db-rebuildable-projection
body:
The DB stays a rebuildable projection. Correctness must never depend on a fresh `apg/.trans/db.lbug`: the next scan can rebuild it from the code, and the durable layers tree can be re-ingested into it. Mutations that do not strictly need the DB must not open it, and must not contend on it.

Code-FQN (`implemented-by`) validation with no projection. `validate_change` today gates the `implemented-by` drift check on `db.lbug`'s existence (src/layers.rs:1868): with a DB present it opens the code universes and rejects a vanished target; with no DB it skips the check. The decoupled path makes this rule explicit and total:
- A projection is present (`apg/.trans/db.lbug` and/or the `apg/.trans/graph.jsonl` export / a cached symbol index): resolve the `implemented-by` target against it and reject a target that is neither a real code FQN nor a declared planned FQN.
- NEITHER the DB NOR `graph.jsonl` nor any index exists: code-FQN `implemented-by` references are NOT validated and the mutation is accepted with the FQN recorded. This is deliberate, not silently weaker than the DB-present path: structural references (edge endpoints, `attaches-to`, contains/depends-on acyclicity, pairing) are ALWAYS validated from the node files, and code identity is a derived-artifact concern — absence of every projection is a valid state, never a failure, and never blocks a durable write. The recorded FQN is re-validated on the next scan, which is authoritative for code identity and surfaces any drift. `graph.jsonl` is normally produced by the same scan as `db.lbug`, so the both-gone case is defined explicitly.

Acceptance: a node/edge mutation path that performs its structural (always) and code-FQN (when a projection is present) reference validation without an exclusive/read-write DB open (or that provably does not contend), plus a test showing a mutation is correct with the DB absent — including the both-artifacts-gone case, where the code FQN is recorded unvalidated and a later scan surfaces any drift.
